complexity.correctness_reason: A skewed (chain) tree of more than ~1000 nodes — permitted by the stated limit of 100,000 nodes — exceeds Python's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError.
complexity.notes: Very terse but idiomatic; using bool-as-int addition for the good-node count is clever though slightly less readable than an explicit conditional. Space is O(h) for the recursion stack, which is O(n) on a skewed tree.
complexity.summary: Recursive DFS carrying the maximum value seen along the root-to-current path; a node is good iff its value is at least that running max, and the results from both subtrees are summed. Each node is visited once.
